about.title: Cloverdale Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Medical malpractice cases in Cloverdale often involve care delivered locally or in nearby Sonoma County facilities where patients expected competent, careful treatment and didn't get it. A missed diagnosis, a surgical mistake, or a medication error can turn a routine visit into a long recovery — sometimes longer than it should have been. California law recognizes that not every bad outcome is malpractice; a claim requires showing that a provider's care fell below an accepted medical standard and that this failure caused real harm. Because these cases involve strict notice requirements, expert review, and firm deadlines, getting informed early matters. LawProactive doesn't practice law or take a cut of any settlement — we simply connect Cloverdale residents with an independent attorney who evaluates the facts and explains what your options may look like. There's no cost to ask, and no obligation to move forward if you're not ready.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Early

items.title: Strict Filing Windows
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from discovering the harm and no more than three years from the injury itself to file — missing that window can end a claim before it starts.

items.title: A Required 90-Day Notice
items.desc: Before suing a healthcare provider, California law requires a 90-day pre-suit notice, which affects timing and strategy from the very beginning.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Needed
items.desc: Because a qualified medical expert typically must confirm the care fell below accepted standards, an attorney familiar with this process can help line up that review early.

items.question: Is every bad medical outcome considered malpractice?
items.answer: No. California law requires showing that a provider's care fell below the accepted medical standard and that this failure directly caused harm. A poor result alone, even a painful or unexpected one, isn't automatically malpractice.

items.question: Do I need to travel outside Cloverdale to get help with this kind of claim?
items.answer: Not necessarily. LawProactive can connect you with an independent attorney who handles Sonoma County medical malpractice matters, and many case reviews and consultations happen remotely or by phone.

items.question: What does California's damages cap mean for my case?
items.answer: California places a statutory cap on non-economic damages, such as pain and suffering, and that cap rises each year under current law. An attorney can walk you through how this applies to your specific circumstances.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything for connecting me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and attorneys in the network generally work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
